ud1.8:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud1.8:1.3: Then at that time venerable Saṅgāmajī had arrived at Sāvatthī to see the Fortunate One.
ud1.8:1.5: “Master Saṅgāmajī it seems has arrived at Sāvatthī”,
ud1.8:1.6: and taking her little boy she went to Jeta’s Wood.
ud1.8:2.1: Then at that time venerable Saṅgāmajī was dwelling for the day sat at the root of a certain tree.
ud1.8:2.2: Then venerable Saṅgāmajī’s former wife went to venerable Saṅgāmajī, and after going, she said to venerable Saṅgāmajī:
ud1.8:2.3: “I have a little son, ascetic, you must take care of me.”
ud1.8:2.4: After that was said, venerable Saṅgāmajī was silent.
ud1.8:3.1: For a second time venerable Saṅgāmajī’s former wife said to venerable Saṅgāmajī:
ud1.8:3.2: “I have a little son, ascetic, you must take care of me.”
ud1.8:3.3: For a second time venerable Saṅgāmajī was silent.
ud1.8:4.1: For a third time venerable Saṅgāmajī’s former wife said to venerable Saṅgāmajī:
ud1.8:4.2: “I have a little son, ascetic, you must take care of me.”
ud1.8:4.3: For a third time venerable Saṅgāmajī was silent.
ud1.8:5.1: Then venerable Saṅgāmajī’s former wife having put the boy down in front of venerable Saṅgāmajī, went away, (saying):
ud1.8:5.2: “This is your son, ascetic, you must take care of him.”
ud1.8:6.1: But venerable Saṅgāmajī did not look at the boy, nor did he speak (to him).
ud1.8:6.2: Then venerable Saṅgāmajī’s former wife, having gone not far away, looking round saw that venerable Saṅgāmajī was neither looking at the boy, nor was he speaking (to him). Having seen (that) this occurred to her:
ud1.8:6.3: “This ascetic does not even have need of a son.”
ud1.8:6.4: Therefore, after turning back and taking the boy, she went away.
ud1.8:6.5: The Fortunate One saw with the divine-eye which is purified, and surpasses that of (normal) men, that venerable Saṅgāmajī’s former wife had such bad manners.
ud1.8:7.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud1.8:8.2: in (her) leaving he does not grieve,
ud1.8:8.3: Saṅgāmajī ‘Victorious in Battle’, free from the shackle:
